910.name: Ancient Arabian Civilizations
910.description: The ancient civilizations of the Arabian Peninsula — the Dilmun on the Gulf, the Mada'in Saleh Nabataeans in the northwest, and the South Arabian incense trade routes through the Hejaz.

sub_clusters.name: Dilmun and Eastern Arabia
sub_clusters.description: The Dilmun civilization's extension into eastern Saudi Arabia, the Tarut Island settlements, copper and pearl trade with Mesopotamia, and the burial mounds of the region.

sub_clusters.name: Lihyanite and Nabataean Northwest
sub_clusters.description: The Lihyanite kingdom at Dedan (Al-Ula), the Nabataean expansion south from Petra to Hegra (Mada'in Saleh), and the magnificent rock-cut tombs of the incense trade route.
key_events: Nabataeans carve the monumental tombs of Hegra (Mada'in Saleh) — now Saudi Arabia's first UNESCO World Heritage Site (1st century BC–1st century AD)

910.name: Pre-Islamic Arabia and Jahiliyyah
910.description: The Arabian Peninsula before Islam — the Kindah and Lakhmid kingdoms, the Kaaba and Meccan trade, Bedouin poetry and tribal society, and the religious landscape of polytheism, Christianity, and Judaism.

sub_clusters.name: Kindah and Arabian Kingdoms
sub_clusters.description: The Kindah confederation of central Arabia, the Lakhmid vassal state of Sassanid Persia, the Himyarite decline in Yemen, and the tribal poetry traditions of the Mu'allaqat.

sub_clusters.name: Mecca and the Quraysh
sub_clusters.description: The Quraysh tribe's custodianship of the Kaaba, Mecca's rise as a commercial and pilgrimage center, the caravan trade networks, and the 'Year of the Elephant' when Abraha's invasion was repelled.
key_events: Year of the Elephant — Abraha's Ethiopian army fails to capture Mecca (c. 570 AD)

910.name: Birth of Islam
910.description: The revelation of the Quran to Prophet Muhammad, the founding of the first Muslim community, the Hijra to Medina, the conquest of Mecca, and the Rashidun Caliphate — the events that shaped world history from the Hejaz.

sub_clusters.name: Prophetic Period in Mecca and Medina
sub_clusters.description: The first revelation on Mount Hira, the persecution in Mecca, the Hijra to Medina (622), the Constitution of Medina, the battles of Badr and Uhud, the conquest of Mecca, and the Farewell Pilgrimage.
key_events: The Hijra — Muhammad migrates from Mecca to Medina, Year 1 of the Islamic calendar (622 AD)
Conquest of Mecca — Muhammad enters Mecca and cleanses the Kaaba (630 AD)
Death of Prophet Muhammad in Medina (632 AD)

sub_clusters.name: Rashidun Caliphate in the Hejaz
sub_clusters.description: The election of Abu Bakr, the Ridda Wars, the rapid Arab conquests under Umar and Uthman, the First Fitna, and the shift of the political center away from the Hejaz to Damascus and Kufa.
key_events: Ridda Wars — Abu Bakr reunifies Arabia under Islam (632–633)
Assassination of Caliph Uthman in Medina triggers the First Fitna (656 AD)

920.name: Hejaz under the Caliphates
920.description: The Hejaz as the spiritual center of Islam but politically peripheral, the Hajj pilgrimage economy, the Umayyad and Abbasid management of the holy cities, and the Carmathian sack of Mecca.

sub_clusters.name: Umayyad and Abbasid Hejaz
sub_clusters.description: The political marginalization of the Hejaz, Husayn's revolt and the tragedy of Karbala, the siege of Mecca by the Umayyads, and the Hajj as the lifeline of the holy cities.
key_events: Siege of Mecca — Umayyad forces damage the Kaaba during the Second Fitna (683 AD)

sub_clusters.name: Carmathian Sack and Sharifs of Mecca
sub_clusters.description: The shocking Carmathian raid on Mecca and theft of the Black Stone, the establishment of the Sharifs of Mecca as hereditary rulers, and the Holy Cities under Fatimid and Ayyubid patronage.
key_events: Carmathians sack Mecca and steal the Black Stone from the Kaaba (930 AD)
Black Stone returned to Mecca after 22 years (952 AD)

920.name: Mamluk and Early Ottoman Arabia
920.description: The Mamluk Sultanate's protection of the Hajj and the Holy Cities, the Ottoman conquest and Suleiman's investment in the Hejaz, and the broader Arabian Peninsula's fragmented tribal politics.

sub_clusters.name: Mamluk Patronage of Holy Cities
sub_clusters.description: The Mamluk Sultanate's lavish patronage of Mecca and Medina, the annual mahmal caravan from Cairo, the Sharifs' balancing between Mamluk patrons and local autonomy.

sub_clusters.name: Ottoman Conquest and Hejaz Province
sub_clusters.description: Selim I's Ottoman conquest of the Mamluk realm, the Ottoman assumption of custodianship of the Two Holy Mosques, and the expansion and beautification of the Haram complexes.
key_events: Ottoman Sultan Selim I accepted as Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques (1517)

930.name: First Saudi State and Wahhabi Movement
930.description: The alliance between Muhammad ibn Saud and Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, the founding of the First Saudi State (Emirate of Diriyah), its dramatic expansion, and destruction by the Egyptian-Ottoman campaign.

sub_clusters.name: The Ibn Saud-Wahhab Pact
sub_clusters.description: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab's religious reform movement, his alliance with Muhammad ibn Saud at Diriyah in 1744, the expansion of the First Saudi State across Najd, and the Wahhabi theological foundations.
key_events: Pact of Diriyah — Muhammad ibn Saud and Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab forge their world-changing alliance (1744)

sub_clusters.name: First Saudi Expansion and Destruction
sub_clusters.description: The Saudi-Wahhabi conquest of Riyadh, the Hejaz, and the shocking sack of Karbala, the Ottoman response, Ibrahim Pasha's Egyptian campaign, and the destruction of Diriyah.
key_events: Saudi-Wahhabi forces capture Mecca and Medina (1803–1806)
Ibrahim Pasha of Egypt captures and destroys Diriyah, ending the First Saudi State (1818)

930.name: Second Saudi State and Rashidi Rivalry
930.description: The revival of Saudi power under Turki ibn Abdullah, the Second Saudi State based in Riyadh, the civil wars, the rise of the Rashidi dynasty of Ha'il, and the Saudi exile in Kuwait.

sub_clusters.name: Second Saudi State
sub_clusters.description: The re-establishment of Saudi rule in Riyadh under Turki and Faisal, internal succession conflicts, the rivalry with the Rashidi dynasty of Ha'il backed by the Ottomans.
key_events: Turki ibn Abdullah recaptures Riyadh and founds the Second Saudi State (1824)

sub_clusters.name: Rashidi Ascendancy and Saudi Exile
sub_clusters.description: The Rashidi capture of Riyadh, the Al-Saud family's exile in Kuwait, the young Abdulaziz (Ibn Saud) plotting to reclaim his patrimony, and the planning of the legendary Riyadh raid.
key_events: Rashidi forces capture Riyadh; Al-Saud family flees to Kuwait (1891)

940.name: Abdulaziz and Unification of Saudi Arabia
940.description: Abdulaziz ibn Saud's legendary recapture of Riyadh, the three-decade campaign to unify the peninsula, the Ikhwan movement and its suppression, the proclamation of Saudi Arabia, and the Aramco oil concession.

sub_clusters.name: Recapture of Riyadh and Nejd Conquest
sub_clusters.description: The dramatic night raid on the Masmak fortress, the reconquest of Nejd, the alliance with Britain during WWI, and the creation of the Ikhwan religious-military settlements.
key_events: Abdulaziz captures the Masmak fortress in Riyadh with a small raiding party (January 15, 1902)

sub_clusters.name: Hejaz Conquest and Kingdom Proclamation
sub_clusters.description: The conquest of Ha'il from the Rashidis, the defeat of Sharif Hussein and conquest of the Hejaz, the Ikhwan rebellion and Battle of Sabilla, and the unification proclamation.
key_events: Abdulaziz conquers Mecca and the Hejaz from the Hashemites (1924–1925)
Battle of Sabilla — Abdulaziz crushes the Ikhwan rebellion (1929)
Kingdom of Saudi Arabia officially proclaimed (September 23, 1932)

sub_clusters.name: ARAMCO Concession and Oil Discovery
sub_clusters.description: The transformative oil concession to Standard Oil of California, the discovery of oil at Dammam No. 7, the ARAMCO relationship, and the revenue that began to reshape the kingdom.
key_events: Dammam No. 7 strikes oil in commercial quantities — Saudi Arabia's first oil well (1938)
Meeting between Abdulaziz and FDR aboard USS Quincy in the Suez Canal (February 1945)

950.name: Oil Kingdom and Cold War Era
950.description: The transformation of Saudi Arabia into the world's dominant oil power, the assassination of King Faisal, the 1973 oil embargo, the Grand Mosque seizure, and the Iran-Iraq War's regional impact.

sub_clusters.name: King Faisal and Oil Embargo
sub_clusters.description: King Faisal's modernizing reign, the abolition of slavery, the 1973 Arab oil embargo's geopolitical shock, OPEC's empowerment, and Faisal's assassination by a nephew.
key_events: 1973 Arab Oil Embargo — Saudi Arabia leads OPEC production cut, quadrupling oil prices
King Faisal assassinated by his nephew (March 25, 1975)

sub_clusters.name: Grand Mosque Seizure and Sahwa
sub_clusters.description: The 1979 Grand Mosque seizure by Juhayman al-Otaybi, the regime's subsequent empowerment of the religious establishment, the Sahwa (Islamic Awakening) movement, and Saudi support for Afghan mujahideen.
key_events: Seizure of the Grand Mosque in Mecca by Juhayman al-Otaybi (November 20, 1979)
Saudi Arabia funds and supports the Afghan mujahideen against the Soviet Union (1979–1989)

950.name: Gulf War and Post-War Tensions
950.description: The stationing of US troops in Saudi Arabia during the Gulf War, the domestic backlash, the rise of Osama bin Laden's opposition, the Khobar Towers bombing, and the September 11 attacks.

sub_clusters.name: US Troops and Domestic Backlash
sub_clusters.description: The controversial invitation to US forces to defend Saudi Arabia, religious opposition to 'infidel' troops near the holy cities, bin Laden's break with the Saudi state, and the 1996 Khobar Towers bombing.
key_events: King Fahd invites US forces to Saudi Arabia — Operation Desert Shield (1990)
Khobar Towers bombing kills 19 US servicemen (June 25, 1996)

sub_clusters.name: Road to September 11
sub_clusters.description: Bin Laden's declaration of war against the United States, the growth of al-Qaeda, and the September 11 attacks perpetrated predominantly by Saudi nationals, transforming US-Saudi relations.
key_events: September 11 attacks — 15 of 19 hijackers are Saudi nationals (September 11, 2001)

960.name: Post-9/11 Reform and Arab Spring
960.description: King Abdullah's cautious reform era, counter-terrorism campaigns, the containment of Arab Spring pressures, women's limited enfranchisement, and intervention in Bahrain.

sub_clusters.name: King Abdullah Reform Era
sub_clusters.description: King Abdullah's scholarship program sending hundreds of thousands abroad, limited municipal elections, the appointment of women to the Shura Council, and the massive social spending to prevent Arab Spring unrest.
key_events: King Abdullah Scholarship Program sends over 200,000 Saudis to study abroad (2005–2019)
Saudi forces enter Bahrain to suppress the Arab Spring uprising (March 2011)

sub_clusters.name: Counter-Terrorism Campaigns
sub_clusters.description: Al-Qaeda's campaign of attacks inside Saudi Arabia, the intensive security crackdown, the deradicalization programs, and the eventual suppression of the domestic militant threat.

960.name: Vision 2030 and MBS Era
960.description: The ascendancy of Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, the ambitious Vision 2030 economic transformation, social liberalization, the Yemen War, the Khashoggi affair, and the NEOM megaproject.

sub_clusters.name: MBS Rise and Social Transformation
sub_clusters.description: Mohammed bin Salman's rapid rise to power, the anti-corruption Ritz-Carlton purge, women's right to drive, the opening of entertainment and cinema, and the Khashoggi murder's diplomatic fallout.
key_events: Women granted the right to drive in Saudi Arabia (June 2018)
Murder of journalist Jamal Khashoggi in the Istanbul consulate (October 2, 2018)

sub_clusters.name: Vision 2030 Megaprojects and Diplomacy
sub_clusters.description: The Saudi Aramco IPO — world's largest, the NEOM futuristic city project, the normalization push with Israel, the China-brokered rapprochement with Iran, and Saudi Arabia's global sporting ambitions.
key_events: Saudi Aramco IPO — world's largest at $29.4 billion (December 2019)
China-brokered Saudi-Iranian diplomatic rapprochement (March 2023)

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
